operations.abstract: Projective Mukai flops of dimension 2m (m>=2) are smooth projective K-equivalences for which push-pull along the smooth common blowup is not fully faithful, although a reducible fiber-product kernel yields derived equivalence.

external_references.exact_result: Example 5.2(2) constructs the smooth projective Mukai flop and its common resolution; Corollary 5.7 gives an equivalence from the reducible correspondence kernel; Proposition 5.12 proves that Rg_{0*}Lf_0^* is not an equivalence for m>=2 by an explicit self-Ext calculation.
external_references.locator: Journal of Differential Geometry 61 (2002), Example 5.2(2), Corollary 5.7, Proposition 5.12, pp. 157-164
external_references.role: Supplies the geometric family and the decisive categorical computation; the blowup canonical-divisor calculation is reproduced in the proof.
external_references.title: D-equivalence and K-equivalence

introduced_notation.definition: Kawamata's smooth projective Mukai flop obtained as a general hypersurface section of a projective standard flop.
The smooth common blowup of the two Mukai-flop centers.
The reducible fiber-product correspondence used by Kawamata as the successful Fourier-Mukai kernel.

operations.proof: Kawamata's Example 5.2(1) starts with the projective standard flop in dimension 2m+1 whose center E is P^m with normal bundle O_{P^m}(-1)^{oplus(m+1)}. Taking a general hypersurface through the unique contraction point gives Example 5.2(2): smooth projective 2m-folds X_0,Y_0 related by a Mukai flop and a smooth common resolution Z_0, with exceptional divisor G_0 and maps f_0,g_0. Here E has codimension m in X_0 and the flopped center F has codimension m in Y_0; f_0 and g_0 are their blowups. The canonical divisor formula for a blowup of a smooth codimension-m center gives K_{Z_0}=f_0^*K_{X_0}+(m-1)G_0=g_0^*K_{Y_0}+(m-1)G_0, proving K-equivalence under the precise hypotheses of ROOT. Let Phi=Rg_{0*}Lf_0^*. Kawamata, Proposition 5.12, takes a=O_{X_0}(-m), computes H^q(Phi(a))=O_{Y_0}(m) for q=0, O_F(-1) for q=m-1, and 0 otherwise, and uses the resulting Ext spectral sequence to show that for 2<=p<=2m-2 the self-Ext groups of a and Phi(a) are not isomorphic. Thus Phi is not fully faithful. On the other hand, Kawamata, Corollary 5.7, proves that the Fourier-Mukai functor with kernel O_{Z'_0}, where Z'_0 is the reducible fiber-product correspondence inherited from the ambient standard flop, is an equivalence. Hence the failed functor cannot disprove derived equivalence, but it rigorously refutes the assertion that equality of pulled-back canonical divisors makes push-pull along an arbitrary smooth common resolution an equivalence.
operations.statement: For every integer m>=2, the projective Mukai-flop construction supplies smooth projective complex varieties X_0 and Y_0 of dimension 2m and a smooth projective common resolution f_0:Z_0->X_0, g_0:Z_0->Y_0 such that f_0^*K_{X_0}=g_0^*K_{Y_0}, but the exact functor Rg_{0*} Lf_0^*:D^b Coh(X_0)->D^b Coh(Y_0) is not fully faithful (hence is not an equivalence). The same X_0 and Y_0 are nevertheless derived equivalent by a Fourier-Mukai kernel supported on the reducible fiber-product correspondence, so this is an obstruction to naive common-resolution descent and not a counterexample to K=>D.

progress_since_previous: Established an explicit higher-dimensional categorical-descent obstruction: in projective Mukai flops the smooth common-resolution push-pull functor can fail even to be fully faithful although a different correspondence kernel gives an untwisted equivalence.
